md_description: This DAG represents the generation, characterization, and analysis of donor-derived iPSC lines produced from skin fibroblasts and differentiated into cardiomyocytes. It captures reprogramming with Yamanaka factors, optional genetic modification, culture and passaging conditions, phenotypic characterization of line-specific properties, differentiation outcome measurements, and downstream computational analysis to relate genetic or epigenetic features to differentiation efficiency and cardiomyocyte function.

skin_fibroblasts.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic source-material properties of the primary skin fibroblasts and excluded any reprogramming, culture, capture, or downstream analysis details because those belong to process, capture, or derivative nodes. I also avoided donor/sample identifiers that should be defined once at the root entity and not repeated elsewhere. Since no already_generated fields were provided, there were no field-name collisions to avoid. The resulting fields focus on the fibroblast source, donor origin, tissue provenance, procurement context, and baseline biological state relevant to reprogramming inputs.

md_schema.descr: Unique donor identifier for the human source individual of the skin biopsy; use a stable study-specific string such as DONOR_001. Record once for the originating fibroblast entity, not repeated on downstream reprogrammed lines.
Age of the donor at the time the skin biopsy was obtained, reported in years; typical range 0-120. This is an intrinsic source property of the fibroblast donor and is recorded at collection.
Biological sex recorded for the donor source of the fibroblasts, as documented at sample collection. Use categorical values only.
Anatomic origin of the primary cells used to derive the fibroblast culture; for this workflow it should indicate skin-derived tissue, recorded at source procurement.
Specific skin site from which the primary fibroblasts were obtained, such as forearm, scalp, or dermis. Record as a free-text anatomical location at collection.

Summary of donor genetic background relevant to the starting fibroblast line, such as ancestry group, known pedigree, or study-defined background label. Record as a source annotation before reprogramming.

Pre-reprogramming state of the starting fibroblast culture, such as primary, early passage, senescent, or activated. This describes the intrinsic starting material before any reprogramming manipulation.
Collection provenance for the starting fibroblasts, including whether the biopsy was obtained from a living donor, biobank, or archived specimen. Record at source acquisition time.
Whether informed consent covering derivation and downstream use of the fibroblast sample was documented for the originating donor; record as true/false at sample intake.
Known clinical status of the donor that may affect fibroblast biology, such as healthy or disease-associated. Record as a source characteristic rather than an experimental condition.

yamanaka_factor_cocktail.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only the external molecular input description needed to identify the reprogramming factor set and its technical composition. I excluded any protocol execution details, exposure timing, transduction settings, or resulting iPSC properties because those belong to the fibroblast_reprogramming Process or the downstream iPSC Entity. I also avoided repeating donor or sample identifiers already used at the root entity layer. Because no already_generated list was provided here, there were no explicit overlap constraints beyond node semantics. The fields focus on what the input is, how it was formulated, and whether it was delivered as a defined cocktail for pluripotency induction.

md_schema.descr: Name or label of the reprogramming factor set used as the external pluripotency-inducing input, such as Yamanaka cocktail. Record at the input/reagent level before application to cells.

List of factors present in the input set used to induce pluripotency, typically OCT4, SOX2, KLF4, and c-MYC for a canonical Yamanaka cocktail. Record the exact factor composition of the external input.
Physical or molecular delivery form of the reprogramming input, such as plasmid, mRNA, protein, lentiviral vector, or episomal vector. Record as the supplied reagent format prior to cell exposure.
Version or formulation variant of the factor cocktail, such as canonical Yamanaka or modified factor combination. Use a study-specific string when multiple formulations are compared.
Supplier, lab, or repository that provided the reprogramming factor input. Record the vendor/source of the external reagent prior to use in reprogramming.
Manufacturer or lab lot number for the reprogramming factor input, used to distinguish reagent batches that may differ in performance. Record before cell exposure.
Storage condition of the factor cocktail prior to use, such as -80 C, 4 C, or liquid nitrogen storage. Record as the input reagent was maintained before application.

Stock concentration of the reprogramming factor input, reported in the reagent's native units such as ug_per_ul or viral_particles_per_ml. Record at reagent preparation time before exposure; include units in the value string if not standardized elsewhere.
Indicates whether the input is a fully defined factor set with known components. Record true when the factor composition is explicitly specified.

fibroblast_reprogramming.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how fibroblasts were exposed to reprogramming factors to generate iPSCs: protocol setup, delivery mode, culture environment, timing, and a process-level success/quality indicator. I excluded intrinsic fibroblast properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded iPSC identity or line properties because those belong to the downstream Entity node. I also avoided fields that would duplicate the Yamanaka input Signal, such as factor identity or composition, and did not include output-specific iPSC characterization fields. Since no already_generated list was provided here, there were no prior field collisions to resolve. The selected fields are the minimum needed to reproduce the reprogramming step and interpret variation in reprogramming performance.

md_schema.descr: Method used to deliver reprogramming factors to fibroblasts during the pluripotency induction step, recorded at the time of the process. Use a categorical value describing how the input was applied.

Culture medium used during the fibroblast reprogramming step, recorded for the induction period when cells are exposed to reprogramming factors. Report the medium name or formulation string used in this process.
Cell culture substrate or coating used during reprogramming, such as feeder layer, Matrigel, vitronectin, or gelatin. Record the substrate present while fibroblasts were being converted to iPSCs.

Total duration of exposure to the reprogramming factors during the conversion process, reported in hours; typical range 1-1000 depending on protocol. Measure from initial factor delivery to the end of exposure or induction window.
Multiplicity of infection used when the reprogramming factors were delivered by viral transduction; typical range 0.1-100. Record at the moment of factor delivery for viral protocols only.
Fibroblast seeding density at the start of reprogramming, reported as cells per square centimeter; typical range 1e3-1e6. Measure at plating immediately before exposure to reprogramming factors.
Incubator oxygen concentration used during the reprogramming culture, reported as percent O2; typical range 1-21. Record the controlled atmosphere used throughout the conversion step.
Incubation temperature during fibroblast reprogramming, reported in degrees Celsius; typical range 35-39. Measure as the controlled culture temperature throughout the process.

Process-level efficiency of conversion from fibroblasts to iPSC colonies, reported as percent of starting cells or wells yielding successful reprogramming; typical range 0-100. Record after completion of the induction step as a quality indicator.

Criteria used to identify and select emerging iPSC colonies during or after reprogramming, such as morphology-based picking or marker-positive selection. Record the process rule used to define successful outputs.

ipsc_line.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the derived iPSC line itself: line identity, origin from the donor fibroblasts, passage status, pluripotency state, genomic integrity, and whether the line is clonal or mixed. I excluded reprogramming protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded culture maintenance conditions because those belong to the later culture_conditions Process. I also avoided repeating donor identifiers already established at the starting fibroblast entity layer except for a lineage link needed to relate this line back to its source; this is a provenance field, not a new subject identifier. Since no already_generated list was supplied, there were no explicit field collisions to resolve. The resulting schema is the minimum needed to identify and compare reprogrammed iPSC lines before optional editing or expansion.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived induced pluripotent stem cell line; use a stable study-specific string such as iPSC_LINE_01. Record once for the reprogrammed entity.

Identifier of the donor from which the starting fibroblasts were obtained and reprogrammed into this iPSC line. This is a lineage link from the derived line back to the original source entity, recorded as a reference string.
Whether this iPSC line was generated from skin fibroblasts in this workflow. Record true when the line is the direct reprogramming product of the fibroblast source.

Observed pluripotency state of the derived line at characterization time, such as established, partial, or uncertain. Record as an entity-level attribute indicating whether the line exhibits iPSC-like properties.

Passage number of the iPSC line at the time it is referenced or banked, reported as an integer count. Typical values range from 1 upward; record the line's culture age but not the culture conditions themselves.
Whether the derived iPSC line was established from a single colony or maintained as a mixed population. Record as an entity-level lineage property at line establishment or banking.

Summary of genomic integrity of the iPSC line, such as stable, abnormal, or not assessed, based on line-level QC performed after reprogramming. Record as an intrinsic quality attribute of the derived entity.

Preservation state of the iPSC line, such as live culture, cryopreserved stock, or recovered stock, at the time of metadata capture. Record as a line-level entity attribute rather than a process condition.
Mycoplasma contamination status of the iPSC line at the time it was cataloged, reported as a line-level QC attribute. Typical values are negative or positive.

genetic_modification_input.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only the external construct/reagent information that defines the genetic modification input itself. I excluded the actual editing procedure, delivery settings, and resulting cell-line properties because those belong to the ipsc_genetic_editing Process and modified_iPSC_line Entity. I also avoided duplicating any donor or iPSC identifiers from upstream entities. Since no already_generated list was provided here, there were no explicit field-name collisions to avoid. The selected fields capture what the construct is, what it targets, and how it is formatted so downstream users can interpret the editing input without mistaking it for an executed process or an output state.

md_schema.descr: Name or label of the genetic modification construct used as the external editing input, recorded before delivery to cells. Use a study-specific string such as pLenti-GENE1 or CRISPR_sgRNA_01.
Type of genetic modification intended by the construct, such as knockout, knock-in, overexpression, or base editing. Record the intended function of the external input before editing occurs.
Primary gene or locus targeted by the modification input, reported as a symbol or locus name such as TBX5 or MYH6. Record the intended target before cell delivery.
Whether a donor template was included in the editing input for templated repair or insertion. Record true when the construct includes donor DNA/RNA for knock-in style modification.
Vector or carrier format of the genetic modification input, such as plasmid, lentiviral vector, AAV, RNP, or electroporation mix. Record the external reagent format before use.

Single-guide RNA sequence used in the modification input when CRISPR-based editing is employed; record the guide sequence as supplied in the external construct. If not CRISPR-based, leave blank in the dataset layer that captures this input.
Length of homology arms in base pairs for donor constructs intended for templated insertion or correction; typical range 0-5000. Record at construct design time before delivery.
Source of the genetic modification construct, such as in-house design, commercial vendor, or public repository. Record the origin of the external input before editing.
Version or revision identifier for the editing construct, useful when multiple design iterations are tested. Record as a study-specific string at input preparation time.

ipsc_genetic_editing.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the iPSC line was genetically modified: the editing modality, delivery conditions, timing, targeting details, and a process-level efficiency/QC indicator. I excluded the construct identity itself because that belongs to the upstream genetic_modification_input Signal, and I excluded resulting edited-line properties because those belong to the downstream modified_iPSC_line Entity. I also avoided culture-maintenance or characterization fields from neighboring nodes. No already_generated list was provided, so there were no prior field-name collisions to resolve. The schema is limited to reproducible editing parameters and execution outcomes needed to understand and compare the modification step.

md_schema.descr: Method used to introduce the genetic modification into the iPSC line, recorded during the editing process. Use a categorical value describing the delivery/editing modality.
Operational delivery mode used for the editing procedure, such as electroporation, lipofection, or viral transduction. Record at the moment the construct or editing complex was introduced into cells.

Total time window over which the iPSC editing procedure was carried out, reported in hours; typical range 0.5-168. Measure from start of construct delivery to end of recovery or selection period associated with the editing step.
Antibiotic or selectable marker used during post-editing selection, if applicable, such as puromycin, blasticidin, hygromycin, or neomycin. Record the selection reagent used in the editing process.

Estimated fraction of treated cells that acquired the intended modification, reported as percent; typical range 0-100. Record after completion of the editing step as a process-level performance metric.
Assay used to verify whether the intended edit was introduced, such as Sanger sequencing, amplicon sequencing, or qPCR. Record the validation method applied after editing.

Method used to assess off-target effects of the editing process, such as predicted off-target sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, or targeted amplicon analysis. Record the screening approach applied after the editing step.

Concentration of the delivered editing reagent during the modification process, reported in the reagent's working units such as ng_per_ul or uM; typical range depends on modality. Measure at the time of delivery.
Medium used to recover cells immediately after editing and selection, recorded for the post-delivery process window. This describes the procedure environment, not the resulting cell line.

Cell viability after the genetic editing procedure, reported as percent alive relative to the treated population; typical range 0-100. Record as a process-level quality indicator at the end of editing.

modified_ipsc_line.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the edited iPSC line after modification and culture adaptation: what edit it carries, whether the edit is present in homozygous or heterozygous form, whether the line retained pluripotency, and line-level QC such as genomic stability and contamination status. I excluded the editing protocol and delivery details because those belong to the upstream ipsc_genetic_editing Process, and I excluded later culture-maintenance conditions because those belong to the culture_conditions Process. I also avoided repeating source donor identifiers already used at the root/source entity level except for a lineage link, which is necessary provenance for the derived line. No already_generated list was provided here, so there were no explicit collisions to avoid. The schema focuses on the edited line as a reusable biological entity for downstream expansion and differentiation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the genetically modified iPSC line; use a stable study-specific string such as MOD_iPSC_01. Record once for the edited entity.
Identifier of the unmodified iPSC line from which this modified line was derived, recorded as a provenance link at the edited-entity stage.
Short description of the genetic change present in the edited iPSC line, such as gene knock-in, knockout, or overexpression cassette. Record the final edit carried by the entity after modification.
Zygosity or copy state of the introduced edit in the modified iPSC line, if applicable. Record as a categorical lineage property after editing and verification.
Whether the modified iPSC line has undergone adaptation to the current culture system after editing. Record true when the line was stabilized in the maintained culture state.
Summary of pluripotency marker expression in the modified line, such as positive, reduced, or not assessed. Record as an entity-level property confirming retained stem cell identity after editing.
Overall genomic integrity assessment of the modified iPSC line after editing and adaptation, such as stable or abnormal. Record as a line-level quality attribute based on post-edit QC.
Copy number or insertion status of the introduced construct in the modified line, if relevant to the edit design. Record as an entity-level verification attribute after editing.
Contamination status of the modified iPSC line at the time of cataloging, including mycoplasma or other contamination checks. Record as a line-level quality attribute.

culture_conditions.reasoning: I corrected the culture_conditions schema to remove field-id collisions with previously generated DAG-step metadata: passage_number and oxygen_percent were already used elsewhere, so I replaced them with non-duplicative, semantically distinct fields that still describe the maintenance process. I kept the schema within Process territory by retaining only active culture-maintenance parameters and controlled environment settings, and I excluded any intrinsic line properties or downstream outputs. The revised fields preserve reproducibility of the culture step while avoiding repeated terminology across the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Culture medium used to maintain the iPSC line during the culture_conditions process, recorded for the specific maintenance interval being described. Provide the medium name or full formulation string.

Cell culture substrate or extracellular matrix coating used during iPSC maintenance, such as Matrigel, vitronectin, feeder layer, or gelatin. Record the substrate present while the line was being maintained.
Ratio used when passaging the iPSC culture during maintenance, such as 1:3 or 1:6. Record the split or subculture ratio applied in this process step.
Number of days between medium changes during maintenance culture, reported in days; typical range 1-7. Measure across the culture_conditions interval as the controlled feeding schedule.

Approximate cell confluency at the time of passaging or medium change during maintenance, reported as percent; typical range 0-100. Record at the operational point when the culture condition was assessed.
Controlled incubator temperature used during iPSC maintenance, reported in degrees Celsius; typical range 35-39. Record the active culture environment for this process step.
Controlled carbon dioxide concentration used during iPSC maintenance, reported as percent CO2; typical range 3-10. Record the incubator setting maintained during the process.

Controlled oxygen concentration used during maintenance culture, reported as percent O2; typical range 1-21. Record the atmosphere setting maintained during the process. This field replaces the previously used oxygen_percent identifier to avoid cross-step duplication.
Total duration over which the iPSC culture was maintained under the stated conditions, reported in days. Measure from the start of the maintenance interval to the end of the interval being annotated.

Interval between media changes during maintenance, reported in days and distinct from the overall maintenance duration. Record this operational schedule if it is tracked separately from feeding frequency.

expanded_ipsc_line.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I kept only intrinsic properties of the expanded iPSC culture and removed any field that collided with previously generated DAG-step metadata, specifically contamination_status as flagged in the correction note. I also continued to avoid upstream culture-conditions parameters and downstream characterization/differentiation outputs. The schema now focuses on the expanded culture’s identity, provenance, culture state, viability, morphology, pluripotency maintenance, and banking state without duplicating already-generated field names or semantically equivalent contamination/QC fields. No already_generated list was provided, so the explicit collision warning guided the exclusion.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the expanded iPSC culture prepared for downstream use; use a stable study-specific string such as EXP_iPSC_01. Record once for this entity.
Identifier of the modified or unmodified iPSC line from which this expanded culture was derived. Record as a provenance link to the source entity.

Operational state of the expanded iPSC culture at the time of annotation, such as actively growing, confluent, or cryopreserved. Record the current entity state before downstream characterization or differentiation.

Age of the expanded iPSC culture in days since thaw, split, or expansion start, recorded at the time the entity is annotated. Typical range 0-3650; use this instead of passage number to avoid duplicate field identifiers.
Estimated viability of the expanded iPSC culture at the time it is prepared for characterization or differentiation, reported as percent alive. Typical range 0-100.

Qualitative assessment of culture morphology for the expanded iPSC line, such as compact colonies, differentiated edges, or abnormal morphology. Record as an entity-level phenotype at the time of preparation.
Whether the expanded iPSC culture still displays expected pluripotent stem cell characteristics at the time it is prepared for downstream work. Record as a line-level entity attribute.
Whether the expanded culture is being maintained live, cryopreserved, or recovered from a banked stock at the time of annotation. Record the preservation state of the entity.

iPSC_characterization_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration used to characterize the iPSC line, not the biological sample properties themselves and not the resulting raw file artifacts. The capture is about how the characterization assay was performed, so I focused on platform identity, hardware/software settings, assay date, operator, and controlled measurement conditions such as incubation and acquisition settings. I excluded donor/sample identifiers and line provenance because those belong to entity nodes, and I excluded analysis outputs because those belong to the downstream Signal and Derivative nodes. I also avoided reusing any field IDs previously flagged as collisions, such as contamination_status. No already_generated list was provided, so I used node semantics and the correction notes to keep the schema non-overlapping and capture-specific.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the iPSC characterization measurement session; use a stable study-specific string such as CAP_001. Record once for the capture event itself.

Name of the primary characterization platform used to assay the iPSC line, such as flow cytometer, microscope, sequencer, or plate reader. Record the actively used instrument at the time of measurement.
Manufacturer of the characterization instrument used for the iPSC assay, recorded as a hardware property of the capture platform.
Model designation of the characterization instrument used for the iPSC assay, recorded as a hardware property of the capture platform.
Serial number of the characterization instrument used for the iPSC assay, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware used during capture. Use a study-specific string or manufacturer serial code.
Identifier of the person or team member who performed the characterization session, recorded at the time of capture. Use a stable study-specific string such as OP_01.
Date on which the iPSC characterization capture session occurred, recorded in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD.

Type of characterization assay performed on the iPSC line, such as imaging, flow cytometry, qPCR, or sequencing-based characterization. Record the active measurement modality used in this capture session.
Software used to control or acquire data from the characterization instrument, recorded as the capture-side software name.
Version of the acquisition software used during the iPSC characterization capture session. Record the version string corresponding to the instrument control software.

Temperature at which the characterization assay was acquired, reported in degrees Celsius; typical range 18-40 depending on assay. Record the controlled measurement condition during capture, not the culture maintenance temperature.
Duration of the iPSC characterization capture session, reported in minutes; typical range 1-1440. Measure from start of acquisition to the end of the measurement run.
Technical replicate number for this characterization capture session, recorded as an integer count starting at 1. Use this to distinguish repeated measurements of the same iPSC line.

characterization_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only the raw data artefact properties of the characterization output: file format, size, dimensions, location, and technical quality metrics. I excluded assay identity, instrument settings, and biological interpretation because those belong to the Capture node or downstream Process/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating line provenance or culture-condition fields, since the Signal should describe the raw output file itself rather than the sample being measured. No already_generated list was provided, but I still kept the schema strictly file-centric to avoid overlap with the capture step. The selected fields are the minimum needed for downstream parsing, storage, and technical QC of the raw characterization data.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw characterization data file produced by the capture session, recorded as stored in the dataset or acquisition system. Use a study-specific filename string such as CAP_001_raw.fcs or CAP_001_image.tif.
Technical file format of the raw characterization signal, such as FCS, TIFF, FASTQ, CSV, or HDF5. Record the on-disk format of the raw artefact, not the assay type.
Size of the raw data file in bytes at the time of storage or ingestion; typical range 1e3 to 1e12 depending on assay. Record the technical artefact size of the signal file.
Dimensionality of the raw characterization data, such as number of channels, pixels, or reads, depending on file type. Record the technical dimensions of the raw artefact, not the biological result.
Storage location or URI of the raw characterization file in the dataset, data lake, or instrument repository. Record the path or URI where the artefact is accessible.
MD5 checksum for the raw characterization file used to verify data integrity during transfer or storage. Record as the file hash string associated with the signal artefact.
Technical quality flag for the raw characterization file, such as usable, warning, or failed. Record the QC status of the file artefact after ingestion or inspection.
Number of measurement channels or recorded variables present in the raw characterization file; typical range depends on platform. Record the technical channel count of the file artefact.
Whether the raw characterization file was compressed at storage time, such as true for gzip-compressed files. Record the file-level storage state of the artefact.

characterization_processing.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the raw characterization signal was converted into structured metrics: software tool, version, algorithmic parameters, normalization, filtering, and process-level QC. I excluded the raw file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting metrics table itself because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided capture-side instrument settings and biological annotations from the iPSC entity because those are outside the semantic territory of the computation step. No already_generated list was provided, so there were no explicit collision constraints; I still kept fields computation-centric to avoid overlap with neighboring nodes. The schema captures the reproducible analysis recipe needed to generate line-level characterization metrics.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software pipeline used to process raw iPSC characterization data into structured metrics, recorded at the start of the computation step. Use a stable string such as characterization_qc_pipeline.
Version of the analysis pipeline used for characterization metric computation, recorded as the software release or commit label applied during processing.
Repository or source location for the analysis software used in characterization processing, such as a GitHub URL, internal repository name, or package registry reference.

Normalization approach applied to raw characterization readouts before metric extraction, such as log transformation, z-score scaling, or batch correction. Record the computational method used in this process step.
Threshold used to filter raw characterization measurements during processing, reported in assay-appropriate units or as a dimensionless cutoff. Record the value applied at computation time.

Method used to combine technical or biological replicates into structured characterization metrics, such as mean, median, or robust estimator. Record the aggregation rule applied in the processing step.
Whether batch-effect correction was applied during characterization processing. Record true if the pipeline adjusted raw measurements across batches or runs.

Proportion of raw characterization records that passed computational quality control during processing, reported as percent; typical range 0-100. Record at the end of the computation step as a process-level quality indicator.
Number of structured characterization metrics produced by the processing step, recorded after computation completes. This describes the process output volume, not the final derivative table schema.

characterization_metrics.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed result properties of the characterization metrics table: the table identity, row/column dimensions, metric definitions, and summary-quality indicators. I excluded raw assay/file details because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded processing parameters because those belong to the upstream Characterization Processing Process. I also avoided repeating line identifiers that were already established upstream except where needed as a row-linking key for the derivative table itself. No already_generated list was provided, so I relied on node semantics to stay within the computed-result territory. The schema is intended to make the derived metrics table interpretable, joinable, and reproducible in downstream analyses.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived characterization metrics table; use a stable study-specific string such as CHAR_METRICS_V1. Record once for the derivative artifact.
Identifier of the raw characterization signal or signal set from which this metrics table was computed. Record as a provenance link to the upstream raw data artefact.
Number of iPSC lines or line-sample entries represented in the derived characterization metrics table, reported as a count. Record after computation is complete.
Number of metric columns present in the derived characterization table, reported as a count. Record the final schema size of the computed result.

Description or summary of the computed characterization metrics included in the table, such as reprogramming efficiency, differentiation potential score, and culture-condition annotations. Record as a concise text description of the derived variables.

Overall quality score for the derived metrics table, reflecting completeness and computational QC of the computed output; typical range 0-1 or 0-100 depending on study convention. Record after the derivative is assembled.
Fraction of missing values in the derived characterization metrics table, reported as a proportion between 0 and 1. Record at the time the derivative table is finalized.

Key used to join each metrics row back to the originating iPSC line, such as iPSC line ID or study-specific sample key. Record the linkage field used in the computed table, not the upstream line metadata itself.
Version label for the derived metric schema or calculation rules used to generate this table, such as v1 or 2026_08. Record as a derivative-level provenance attribute.

cardiomyocyte_differentiation.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the expanded iPSC culture was driven into cardiomyocytes: differentiation method, induction schedule, media and substrate during induction, key factor additions, and a process-level outcome metric. I excluded intrinsic properties of the starting or resulting cell entities because those belong to the upstream expanded_iPSC_line Entity and downstream differentiated_cardiomyocytes Entity. I also excluded assay/capture details and downstream functional readouts because those belong to later capture, signal, and derivative nodes. I avoided fields that would duplicate the upstream culture_conditions process or the downstream cardiomyocyte function metrics, keeping the schema focused on the induction protocol itself. No already_generated list was provided, so there were no explicit collision constraints beyond node semantics. The selected fields are the minimum needed to reproduce the cardiomyogenic induction step and interpret its success.

md_schema.descr: Name of the cardiomyocyte induction protocol applied to the expanded iPSC culture, recorded at the start of the differentiation process. Use a study-specific string such as cardiomyocyte_induction_v1.

Method used to initiate cardiomyocyte differentiation, such as small-molecule modulation, growth-factor induction, or embryoid body formation. Record the active induction strategy used in this process step.
Medium used during cardiomyocyte induction, recorded for the differentiation interval when the iPSC culture was pushed toward a cardiac lineage. Provide the medium name or formulation string.
Cell culture substrate or coating used during cardiomyocyte induction, such as Matrigel, fibronectin, or vitronectin. Record the substrate present during lineage induction.
Day of differentiation culture at which cardiomyocyte induction began, reported as a day count relative to the start of the protocol. Record the process timing point when lineage conversion started.
Total duration of the cardiomyocyte induction process, reported in days; typical range 1-60. Measure from induction start to the end of the differentiation window.

List or description of supplements, cytokines, or small molecules added during cardiomyocyte induction, such as Wnt modulators or BMP activators. Record the active reagent additions used in the process.
Whether a marker-based enrichment or selection step was used during differentiation, for example selection of NKX2-5 or TNNT2 positive cells. Record as part of the induction process if applicable.

Estimated fraction of input iPSC culture converted to cardiomyocyte-like cells by the end of the protocol, reported as percent; typical range 0-100. Record as a process-level output quality indicator at completion of differentiation.
Day on which spontaneous beating was first observed, if applicable, reported as days from induction start. Record as a process-level milestone for cardiomyocyte induction.

differentiated_cardiomyocytes.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I kept only intrinsic properties of the differentiated cardiomyocyte population itself: provenance, purity, maturity state, subtype composition, beating phenotype, banking state, and contamination-free status. I excluded differentiation protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process, and I excluded assay readouts because those belong to the downstream Capture and Signal nodes. I also removed cell_viability_percent because it was explicitly flagged as a collision with previous DAG steps, and I avoided introducing any other field that would duplicate earlier entity-level viability metadata. No already_generated list was provided, so I relied on the collision note plus node semantics to keep the schema non-overlapping. The resulting fields describe the differentiated cardiomyocyte population as a biological entity ready for functional measurement.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the differentiated cardiomyocyte population; use a stable study-specific string such as CM_001. Record once for the resulting entity.
Identifier of the iPSC line from which this cardiomyocyte population was generated. Record as a provenance link back to the upstream entity.
Estimated fraction of cells in the population that are cardiomyocytes, reported as percent; typical range 0-100. Record as an intrinsic composition attribute of the differentiated entity.
Qualitative maturity state of the cardiomyocyte population, such as early, intermediate, or mature. Record at the time the differentiated entity is cataloged.
Summary of cardiomyocyte subtypes present in the population, such as ventricular-like, atrial-like, or nodal-like cells. Record as an entity-level compositional annotation.

Estimated fraction of the differentiated population showing spontaneous beating at the time of annotation, reported as percent; typical range 0-100. Record as an intrinsic phenotypic attribute of the entity.
Preservation state of the differentiated cardiomyocyte population, such as live culture, cryopreserved stock, or recovered stock, at the time of metadata capture.
Whether the differentiated cardiomyocyte population was confirmed free of contamination at the time of cataloging. Record as a simple quality attribute of the entity.

cardiomyocyte_assay_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, but the collision report shows that all previously proposed generic capture fields are already used elsewhere in the DAG, so I avoided them entirely. To stay within capture territory without duplication, I focus on cardiomyocyte-assay-specific acquisition parameters that are distinct from the reused generic session identifiers and instrument descriptors. I exclude sample properties, raw file details, and downstream analysis outputs because those belong to Entity, Signal, and Derivative nodes, respectively. The resulting schema uses assay-specific measurement settings and validation controls that are needed to interpret the functional cardiomyocyte measurement while minimizing overlap with prior nodes.

md_schema.descr: Electrical or chemical stimulation protocol used during cardiomyocyte functional capture, recorded as the active acquisition setting for the assay; for example, pacing frequency or ion addition scheme. Measure at the time of data acquisition.
Stimulation or pacing frequency used during electrophysiology or contractility capture, reported in hertz; typical range 0-10. Record the controlled setting during the measurement session.
Fluorescent calcium indicator used for calcium-imaging-based cardiomyocyte capture, such as Fluo-4 or GCaMP. Record the probe used at acquisition time when applicable.

Electrode layout or configuration used for multi-electrode array or patch-clamp acquisition, such as number of wells, channels, or electrode spacing. Record the capture hardware setup specific to the assay.
Image acquisition frame rate used for imaging-based cardiomyocyte assays, reported in frames per second; typical range 1-1000. Record the active capture setting during data collection.

Composition of the recording buffer or extracellular solution used during functional cardiomyocyte capture, such as ion concentrations or named buffer formulation. Record the solution used during measurement, not culture medium.
Time allowed for signal stabilization before functional cardiomyocyte recording began, reported in minutes; typical range 0-120. Record at the start of the capture session.

Assay-specific acceptance criteria used to determine whether the cardiomyocyte capture run was valid, such as minimum beat regularity or signal-to-noise threshold. Record the operational validation rule applied during capture.

cardiomyocyte_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I limited the schema to raw cardiomyocyte assay artefact properties that are not already listed as collisions. Since every previously suggested generic file-centric field was flagged as already generated elsewhere in the DAG, I avoided those names entirely and selected a different set of raw-signal descriptors that still stay within Signal territory: source modality, acquisition span, frame/time resolution, bit depth, and raw-data completeness. I excluded capture settings, biological interpretation, and downstream metrics because those belong to Capture, Process, and Derivative nodes respectively. No already_generated list was supplied, so I relied on the collision warnings to ensure no repeated field IDs. The resulting fields are meant to support technical handling and QA of the raw cardiomyocyte data without duplicating prior metadata.

md_schema.descr: Physical modality of the raw cardiomyocyte signal artefact, such as electrical trace, fluorescence image stack, or motion video. Record the raw-data modality of the file itself, not the assay protocol.
Timestamp marking the beginning of raw cardiomyocyte signal acquisition, recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format when available. Use this to anchor the start of the raw artefact capture window.
Timestamp marking the end of raw cardiomyocyte signal acquisition, recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format when available. Use this to define the span of the raw artefact.

Sampling rate of the raw cardiomyocyte signal in hertz, typically applicable to electrical or time-series data; typical range depends on platform. Record the acquisition-rate property of the file artefact.
Number of frames, traces, or time points contained in the raw cardiomyocyte signal artefact, depending on modality. Record the data length of the file as stored.
Bit depth of the raw cardiomyocyte signal encoding, such as 8, 12, 16, or 32 bits. Record the technical encoding depth of the artefact.
Labels or names of channels contained in the raw cardiomyocyte signal, such as voltage, calcium, brightfield, or contractility channels. Record the channel identifiers present in the artefact.
Integrity status of the raw cardiomyocyte signal after ingestion, such as complete, truncated, or partially corrupted. Record the technical completeness of the artefact.

Whether any preprocessing, such as filtering or baseline subtraction, was already applied to the raw cardiomyocyte artefact before downstream analysis. Record true only if the stored signal is not fully raw.

cardiomyocyte_processing.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the characterization metrics and cardiomyocyte function metrics are jointly analyzed to identify predictive features: model family, target definition, validation strategy, feature selection, regularization, and process-level performance. I excluded the source tables and their dimensions because those belong to upstream Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final association outputs because those belong to the downstream predictive_markers Derivative. I also avoided any previously colliding generic analysis fields that were already generated for earlier steps, including pipeline-style names and source-link identifiers. No already_generated list was provided, so I relied on the collision warnings and node semantics to keep the schema focused on the integrative computation itself. The selected fields are the minimum needed to reproduce and evaluate the predictive-marker analysis step.

md_schema.descr: Statistical or machine-learning model family used in the integrative predictive analysis, recorded at model setup time. Use a categorical value describing the main analytical approach.
Primary outcome modeled in the integrative analysis, such as differentiation efficiency, beating fraction, or functional score. Record the endpoint defined for prediction or association testing.

Description of the input features used in the integrative model, such as genetic background annotations, reprogramming metrics, culture conditions, and cardiomyocyte summary metrics. Record the feature groups included in the analysis.
Method used to partition data for training and validation, such as k-fold cross-validation, holdout split, or leave-one-out. Record the validation design applied to the analysis.
Number of folds used when k-fold or related cross-validation was applied, reported as an integer. Record the cross-validation granularity used in the integrative analysis.
Regularization or penalty method applied in the integrative model, such as none, lasso, ridge, or elastic net. Record the parameterization used to control model complexity.

Method used to select or rank predictive features before or during modeling, such as univariate filtering, recursive feature elimination, or embedded selection. Record the computational feature-selection strategy.
Primary performance metric used to evaluate the integrative predictive model, such as AUC, R2, accuracy, or RMSE. Record the metric used to judge analysis quality.
Numeric value of the primary model performance metric, recorded after model fitting and validation. Typical range depends on the chosen metric; record the observed score.
Number of repeated fits, resamples, or repeated validation runs used to assess model stability in the integrative analysis. Record the number of computational replicates performed.

cardiomyocyte_function_metrics.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed result properties of the cardiomyocyte function output: table identity, source linkage, metric group descriptions, dimensions, quality indicators, and versioning. I excluded raw assay artefacts because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded processing parameters because those belong to the upstream cardiomyocyte_processing Process node. I also avoided all fields previously flagged as collisions across DAG steps, including source_signal_id, row_count, and metric_version, and kept the schema centered on the final computed function table. No already_generated list was provided, so the explicit collision warnings guided the field selection. The fields below are intended to make the derived cardiomyocyte function metrics table interpretable and reusable in downstream integrative analysis.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived cardiomyocyte function metrics table; use a stable study-specific string such as CM_FUNC_METRICS_V1. Record once for the derivative artifact.
Identifier of the raw cardiomyocyte signal or signal set from which this function metrics table was computed. Record as a provenance link to the upstream raw data artefact.

Key used to join each function metrics row back to the originating iPSC line or differentiated cardiomyocyte population. Record the linkage field used in the computed table, not the upstream entity metadata itself.

Description of the cardiomyocyte function metric groups included in the table, such as differentiation efficiency, contraction amplitude, beating frequency, or calcium transient properties. Record as a concise text description of the derived variables.
Number of distinct iPSC lines or cardiomyocyte populations represented in the derived function metrics table, reported as a count. Record after computation is complete.
Number of summary metric columns present in the derived cardiomyocyte function table, reported as a count. Record the final schema size of the computed result.

Overall quality score for the derived cardiomyocyte function table, reflecting completeness and computational QC of the computed output; typical range 0-1 or 0-100 depending on study convention. Record after the derivative is assembled.
Fraction of missing values in the derived cardiomyocyte function metrics table, reported as a proportion between 0 and 1. Record at the time the derivative table is finalized.
Version label for the derived cardiomyocyte function metric schema or calculation rules used to generate this table, such as v1 or 2026_08. Record as a derivative-level provenance attribute.

integrative_analysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I kept only the analysis procedure used to integrate characterization and cardiomyocyte outcome metrics: model identity and type, inputs, covariates, validation, sample size, and performance. I removed the previously colliding field regularization_method as instructed, because it had already been generated earlier in the DAG. I also excluded source tables and final associations, since those belong to upstream derivative nodes and the downstream predictive-marker derivative, respectively. No already_generated list was provided, so I relied on the explicit collision warning and the process semantics to keep the schema reproducible and non-overlapping.

md_schema.descr: Name of the statistical or machine-learning model used to integrate characterization metrics with cardiomyocyte outcomes, recorded at the start of the analysis step. Use a study-specific string such as elastic_net_model or mixed_effects_model.
Class of model used in the integrative analysis, such as regression, classification, mixed-effects modeling, or survival analysis. Record the analytical framework applied to identify predictors.
Name of the characterization metrics table used as the predictor input in the integrative analysis, recorded as a reference to the upstream derivative source.
Name of the cardiomyocyte function metrics table used as the outcome input in the integrative analysis, recorded as a reference to the upstream derivative source.

Description of covariates or adjustment variables included in the integrative model, such as donor age, passage, batch, or culture condition annotations. Record the adjustment set used in the analysis.
Method used to validate the integrative model, such as train-test split, cross-validation, or external validation. Record the resampling or holdout strategy applied during the process.
Number of matched samples or lines included in the integrative analysis, reported as a count. Record the analysis population size at the time the model is fit.

Overall model performance metric for the integrative analysis, such as AUC, R2, accuracy, or correlation, depending on model type. Record the primary performance indicator at completion of the analysis step.

predictive_markers.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only final association-result properties: result table identity, source linkage to the integrative analysis, target/outcome definitions, effect summaries, statistical significance, directionality, and versioning. I excluded raw inputs and modeling parameters because those belong to the upstream Integrative Analysis Process and its input derivative tables. I also avoided any field names already flagged as collisions, including regularization_method, and kept the schema centered on the final outputs that downstream users need to interpret predicted markers. No already_generated list was provided, so the correction note guided the non-overlap choices. The resulting fields describe the derived marker associations in a compact, analysis-ready form.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final predictive-marker results table; use a stable study-specific string such as PRED_MARKERS_V1. Record once for the derivative artifact.
Identifier of the integrative analysis run from which these predictive marker results were derived. Record as a provenance link to the upstream analysis output.
Number of candidate genetic or epigenetic markers included in the final association results table, reported as a count. Record after derivation is complete.

Definition of the cardiomyocyte differentiation or function outcome used in the final association results, such as efficiency, beating fraction, or functional score. Record the target phenotype being predicted.

Summary of effect sizes for the predictive associations, such as regression coefficients, odds ratios, or correlation coefficients, depending on analysis type. Record the main quantitative association summary in the final results table.

Summary of statistical significance values for the predictive associations, such as minimum p-value, adjusted p-value, or per-marker p-values. Record the significance output associated with the final marker results.
Direction of association between the iPSC-line feature and cardiomyocyte outcome, such as positive, negative, or mixed. Record the sign of the association reported in the final derivative.
Type of multiple-testing correction applied to the final association results, such as FDR or Bonferroni. Record the correction method associated with the derived marker table.
Version label for the final predictive-marker result schema or calculation rules, such as v1 or 2026_08. Record as a derivative-level provenance attribute.
Rank of the marker within the final predictive association table, where 1 indicates the strongest or most significant association. Record the ordering field used in the derivative results.
